newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU summit on reform, EMU pact opens.
newsitem.headline: EU summit on reform, EMU pact opens.

text.p: A European Union summit meant to reform the 15-nation bloc in preparation for admitting new east European members opened on Monday, overshadowed by a dispute over the conditions for a single European currency.

The summit began at the Dutch central bank headquarters in Amsterdam after finance ministers narrowed differences on Sunday night over French demands for new measures to promote growth and jobs alongside a controversial pact limiting budget deficits.

EU finance ministers were to meet separately at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT) to try to wrap up an agreement on the stability pact and jobs resolution, which summit leaders were due to address at 5 p.m. (1500 GMT) after a day discussing institutional reform.
After Sunday night's informal dinner talks, Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said ministers had made "extremely good progress" on the stability pact and forecast agreement on a text on Monday.
With financial markets watching, Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinifto told Reuters that big steps had been taken and it was "quite obvious" there would an agreement on Monday.

France's new Socialist government stunned its partners last Monday by requesting a delay to review the deficit-limiting pact and insisting that equal weight be given to coordinating EU economic policies to promote growth and jobs.
